To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified the introgression segments associated with resistance to the basal stalk rot disease caused by Sclerotiinia sclerotiorium from two wild Helianthus annuals species.

introgressions from two wild Helianthus species, H. argophylus and H. petitolaris, were identified and associated with resistance to basal stalk rot, and a downy mildews resistance gene, Pl 17, was also integrated into some of the introgression lines.

we developed eight introgression lines with high levels of resistance to Sclerotiinia basal stalk rot from H. argophilus and H. peltolaris, and identified the introgressed segments in linkage groups 3, 9, and 11 associated with BSR in H. argophilous, and linkage groups 3 and 8 associated with BSR from H. peltoralis.

the transfer of Sclerotinia basal stalk rot resistance from wild Helianthu argophyllus into cultivated sunflower using a marker-assisted breeding approach, and the identification of introgressed alien chromosomal segments associated with resistance.
the transfer of BSR resistance from H. argophyillus and H. petiolars into cultivated sunflower.
the development of sunflower introgression lines with resistance to Sclerotinia BSR, and the identification of introgressed alien regions associated with the resistance using GBS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the introgression lines with the alien segments derived from H. argophytes and H. petiolaris are highly resistant to Sclerotina BSR and could be used in the sunflower breeding program.

this study demonstrates the potential of using GBS to transfer BSR and downey mildew resistance from wild annual species to cultivated sunflower and to identify the introgressions associated with these resistances.
the GBS approach has been successfully used to identify the introgression segments associated with BSB resistance and to develop the introgression lines for further sunflower breeding and research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the BSR resistance derived from the wild species, H. argophylus and H. Petiolaris, was transferred into cultivated sunflower, and the introgressed segments associated with BRS resistance were successfully identified using a GBS approach.
the GBS approach was successfully applied to detect the introgression regions associated with Sclerotina BSR resistance from H. argophyillus and H. petiolaris.

the GBS approach was successfully used for the detection of introgressed alien genomic segments associated with BSN resistance in the introgression sunflower lines derived from the wild species, and the introgressed segments in LGs 3, 9, and 11 were identified for the first time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the wild species can be an effective source of resistance to Sclerotionia BSR in cultivated sunflower, and that GBS is a powerful tool to identify alien segments associated with disease resistance.

the introgression lines derived from the crosses of H.arg and H.pet with cultivated sunflower have high levels of resistance to Sclerotiina BSR and can serve as valuable sources of resistance in sunflower breeding.
